title: Cams and cranks
prompt: A labelled principle teaching rig based on pages 48 and 49 compares a profiled cam with a spring-return guided follower and a separate crank disk with an offset pin, connecting rod and guided slider. Rotate drives each shaft and shows the two conversions from rotation to reciprocation. Swap cam stops the rig and exchanges a real removable cam profile to compare lift and timing. Drive slider applies external motion to the crank slider to demonstrate reverse conversion into rotation through complete cycles. See-through reveals the contact surface, spring, guides and pin joints. Identify the interchangeable rig as a teaching adaptation, not the mammoth machine or a complete engine.
blurb: A principle teaching adaptation compares spring-return cam contact with pinned crank geometry and reverse conversion.

adaptation.deadCentre: Disk inertia carries dead centres; slider force cannot start the disk at an exact dead centre.

sourceEvidence.2016: Saved primary page text and page 49 image read
